# Reinforcement learning for Nemotron Transcribe

Turn the model's better sampled answers into a better model. Start with a small sample of customer audio, measure
whether useful alternatives exist, then train on recordings that expose those alternatives. Success is a better
held-out task score with acceptable retention—not a higher training reward.

The default seed is [`nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B).
Use its full Hugging Face snapshot, including the tokenizer, speech encoder, projection and auxiliary heads.
This skill uses NeMo-Speech, NeMo-RL and NeMo-Automodel.

## References

Paths beginning with `examples/` are relative to the Speech checkout. `$RL` means the separate NeMo-RL checkout.

| When | Read |
|---|---|
| Preparing rows, prompts and rollout selection | [Data and signal](references/data-and-signal.md) |
| Choosing a reward or a small-task preset | [Tasks and presets](references/tasks-and-presets.md) |
| Installing, launching, exporting and evaluating | [Execution](references/execution.md) |
| Running a small Mandarin–English experiment | [ASCEND end-to-end example](references/ascend-example.md) |
| Understanding the underlying GSPO recipe | [NeMo-RL SpeechLM guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL/blob/main/docs/guides/gspo-speechlm.md) |
| Reusing dataset preparation and task scoring | `examples/speechlm2/finetuning/README.md`, `task_metrics.py` in that directory |
| Choosing SFT when RL has no useful signal | `../finetune-speech-llm/SKILL.md` |

## 1. Define the experiment

Collect what is missing; use information the customer already supplied. Write a short run plan and continue within
the agreed compute budget. Do not require a separate approval round for every stage.

| Input | Record |
|---|---|
| Seed | HF repository, immutable revision and downloaded snapshot |
| Training data | Labeled audio, source/version, usable split and any language/domain balance |
| Development data | Data for prompt, hyperparameter and checkpoint decisions |
| Evaluation data | Held-out final measurement; never used for mining or checkpoint selection |
| Task and prompts | Desired output, user instruction(s), reference conventions and language information allowed at inference |
| Objective | Primary metric, target improvement, protected tasks/classes and acceptable degradation |
| Resources | GPU type/count, time/step limit, storage, scheduler and existing compatible image/environment |

Ask for a retention dataset when preserving another capability matters. If none is available, state that retention
will remain unmeasured. If splits are missing, create them from training material before sampling; separate speakers
or recordings where possible. Check audio identity and overlapping recording segments across splits, not just filenames.

Keep `plan.md`, `progress.md` and a compact experiment ledger in the customer work directory. Record source commits,
resolved configs, data membership, prompt text, metric code and output paths. Record failures as well as successes.

## 2. Establish a useful baseline

1. Compare a few references with greedy seed outputs. Resolve wrong language, script, label vocabulary, number style
   or prompt/reference mismatch before interpreting the error rate.
2. If no prompt is established, compare a few plausible prompts **on development data**. Keep the system message
   empty and put the user instruction before audio, as required by the native ASR processor. For a focused task,
   prefer one prompt; use prompt variation when robustness to several deployment instructions is itself a goal.
3. Freeze the chosen prompt, scoring/normalization, decoding settings and selection criterion. Measure the seed on
   development and retention data. A seed test decode may be cached, but do not inspect it to tune the experiment.
4. For label tasks, also establish a development-fitted no-training comparator when aliases, label priors or output
   parsing explain many errors. Apply the same allowed post-processing to compared models. Report strict and parsed
   results separately. An RL gain over a poorly prompted seed is not necessarily a gain over this comparator.

Report error-rate reduction as `(seed_error - candidate_error) / seed_error`; it is not a relative increase in
accuracy. For nearly perfect baselines, report error counts and uncertainty rather than an unstable percentage.

## 3. Find useful training signal

Read [Data and signal](references/data-and-signal.md). Reuse compatible cached rollouts first. Otherwise sample a
small, shuffled, stratified subset of the **training split** and decode a greedy answer plus eight stochastic answers
per recording. Use the intended training prompt and reward, temperature 0.8, and sufficient output/context limits.

Summarize by task/language/domain:

- valid completed responses, truncation/failure rate and cost;
- groups with different rewards, their spread, and groups containing an answer better than greedy;
- all-correct, all-wrong and mixed groups for binary tasks;
- representative actual errors: substitutions, omissions, repetitions, empty outputs, label confusions or code switches.

Extend uncertain, useful strata to 16 samples; use 32–64 only when the expected extra yield justifies it. Eight mining
samples and 64 online training samples serve different purposes. An all-equal eight-sample group is weak evidence,
not proof that all future responses will be identical.

Select useful contrast without demanding a perfect answer or a catastrophic alternative. Keep source/language and
protected-task coverage; avoid filling the dataset solely with the largest reward gaps. Small differences created
only by normalization quirks are not useful task signal. The oracle best-of-samples score is an opportunity estimate,
not an expected trained-model score.

To improve task/domain X while preserving Y, include representative **training data from both** in the RL mix.
Keep development and evaluation examples out of that mix. Mine useful reward variation in each domain and track
their actual retained groups; merely evaluating Y, or adding Y examples whose rewards are all equal, supplies no
retention learning signal. Adjust the mixture using development results for both X and Y.

If meaningful contrasts are scarce, inspect reward correctness, references and prompts, then sample a different
training stratum. If the model still cannot produce useful answers, explain the evidence and recommend SFT or new
data. Do not spend a long RL run trying to manufacture a capability absent from its samples.

## 4. Choose the smallest informative run

Read [Tasks and presets](references/tasks-and-presets.md). Start from the public native SpeechLM GSPO config and
change data, task reward, prompt, LR/step budget and evaluation cadence deliberately. Preserve the tested optimizer,
update surface, precision, synchronous rollout/refit, dropout behavior and exporter for the first comparison.

- Default starting LR: `1e-6`, five-update warmup, then constant. Small tasks: 20 updates first; at most 100 in the
  initial comparison. Export/evaluate every 10–20 updates. These are starting settings, not a promised improvement.
- Preserve 64 online responses per recording and 20 retained groups per update initially. The recipe offers 40
  groups, then takes the first 20 with nonconstant rewards; it does **not** rank and take the “20 best” groups.
- At 20 retained groups, 100 updates mean 2,000 group presentations and 128,000 response presentations, with possible
  repeated audio. Decoding discarded/refill groups costs extra. A selected 500–1,000-recording pool can be sufficient
  for a small study; count actual distinct contributors rather than demanding a large dataset up front.
- Preserve the recipe's explicit 269 trainable tensors / 1,074,318,400 scalars for this model. CTC, MTP, routers,
  experts and the output head remain frozen. Keep trainable storage FP32; serving storage is a separate contract.
- Four eight-GPU nodes are the reference training layout. More nodes do not automatically change batch size.
  Changing the 20×64 batch is a separate experiment that also changes sample exposure and may require an LR comparison.

Size context/output limits from the actual audio and task. A short label may need only 16 output tokens; a transcript
may need thousands. Never copy a classification cap into ASR or treat a tokenizer-only prompt length as audio-expanded
context length. Keep the data loader's epoch allowance large enough to reach the step budget, and stop on the step limit.

## 5. Train and use early results

Follow [Execution](references/execution.md). Record the fully resolved config; the YAML inherits defaults. Start
the bounded run in a fresh output directory. A restart from that directory is a resume, not a new seed comparison.

Use the first updates to inspect the actual run while training proceeds:

- Correct seed and update surface loaded; CTC is frozen; rewards, log probabilities, advantages and loss are finite.
- Correct audio/prompt grouping, nonzero loss masks and aligned **retained** rewards. Use `filtered_rewards` where
  available: raw offered-batch `rewards` may not align with retained row IDs.
- Retained groups and distinct contributing recordings by task/class, cumulative repeats, refill cost and throughput.
  Homogeneous “retention anchors” receive zero advantage; their presence in the manifest does not protect a capability.
- Checkpoint exports decode with the same prompt, scorer and serving settings as the seed. Retention/class recall
  can deteriorate while aggregate reward improves.

For retained group size G, the tested estimator subtracts the other G−1 rewards' mean, then divides by the full
group's sample standard deviation plus epsilon. Sequence-level clipped importance ratios weight these advantages.
Do not substitute a different estimator, reward clipping or KL penalty while debugging data selection.

If refills dominate, inspect which strata still have contrast and refresh the training-only selection. If reward
improves but dev quality does not, inspect paired outputs and the scoring contract before adding steps. If protected
classes or retention exceed the agreed tolerance, keep the earlier acceptable checkpoint and diagnose the change.
Do not silently extend the budget or change the metric to make a run look successful.

## 6. Select, evaluate and hand over

Choose the checkpoint on the predeclared development metric subject to retention/class constraints; include the seed
as a valid outcome. Export that checkpoint canonically, then evaluate it and the seed on the untouched evaluation
split under the same conditions. If the evaluation set has already influenced development, label it a reused benchmark.

Report overall and relevant slice metrics, error counts and paired changes. ASR needs insertion/deletion/substitution,
empty-output and repetition diagnostics; code switching needs monolingual and mixed slices; classification needs
macro recall, per-class recall, confusion and invalid-output rates. Use paired uncertainty estimates when the gain
is small. Frozen CTC weights do not establish timestamp retention when the speech encoder was updated.

Deliver a short result table plus exact commands, resolved config, selected data/rollout provenance, native checkpoint
and HF export paths, prompt/metric definitions, compute consumed, and the next justified action. Clearly distinguish
measured gains, unsuccessful trials and settings that have not been tested on the customer's stack.

# Train a DFlash speech draft

Use `examples/speechlm2/dflash_train.py` with `examples/speechlm2/conf/dflash.yaml`.
This trains a separate draft; the entire SALM target, including its audio encoder and modality projection, stays frozen.
The ordinary `salm_train.py` entry point does not enable draft training.

Read these repository sources as needed; paths below are relative to the repository root:

- `docs/source/speechlm2/dflash_training.rst`: supported configuration, labels, warm starts, and projection-only training.
- `examples/speechlm2/conf/dflash.yaml`: current draft defaults; inherits target/data/trainer settings from `salm_automodel.yaml`.
- `nemo/collections/speechlm2/parts/dflash.py`: audio expansion, feature capture, packing, losses, and export.
- `docs/source/speechlm2/vllm_dflash.rst`: serving setup and draft architecture registration.
- `docs/source/starthere/install.rst` and `pyproject.toml`: training environment and pinned Automodel dependency.

## 1. Establish the experiment

Reuse the user's specified target, draft, data, and compute allocation. Identify any missing checkpoint paths,
training budget, and evaluation set before launching work that depends on them. Record the Speech and Automodel
revisions, resolved config, target/draft paths, data blend, seed, and output directory with the job.

Keep three checkpoint roles separate:

| Setting | Role | State restored |
|---|---|---|
| `model.init_from_checkpoint` | Frozen audio-conditioned SALM target | Target weights |
| `dflash.init_from_pretrained` | Local, compatible HF draft export | Draft weights only; fresh optimizer/scheduler/steps |
| `exp_manager.resume_from_checkpoint` | Interrupted DFlash training run | Draft and training state, including optimizer/scheduler/steps |

Use a new `exp_manager.explicit_log_dir` for an independent experiment. The inherited recipe enables auto-resume;
disable `exp_manager.resume_if_exists` for a fresh run so old checkpoints cannot silently override a warm start.
For a continuation, verify the resumed global step and optimizer/scheduler state rather than treating an HF export
as a full training checkpoint. Keep the same frozen target and trainable parameter selection when resuming.

## 2. Match both architectures

Read the target's saved config and tokenizer metadata. Derive the `model` settings from that target's known working
SALM recipe, including encoder/adapter type, language backbone, tokenizer paths, prompt format, and audio token
estimator. Merely setting `model.init_from_checkpoint` does not replace the inherited model architecture.
Keep strict target initialization enabled; investigate missing parameters instead of disabling it to make a run start.

For a warm start, read the draft's `config.json` and match its hidden size, layer count, attention/MLP dimensions,
rotary settings, target-layer taps, mask token, and DFlash2 convolution/selector settings. Strict loading checks tensor
coverage and shapes, but cannot detect every semantic mismatch, such as different same-shaped layer taps.
Use a trainable floating-point draft export; the packed NVFP4 inference artifact cannot directly initialize this
BF16 training path. A null `dflash.init_from_pretrained` initializes a fresh draft, not pretrained weights.

The shipped recipe has six draft layers and target taps `[1, 5, 19, 29, 41, 51]`. These are zero-based target block
outputs captured before the final norm, not six copies of the final layer. Do not transfer these IDs to a different
backbone without checking its depth and the draft's feature contract.

Supported topology is target `tp_size=pp_size=cp_size=1`, with draft DP/FSDP and compatible target EP.
Set topology for the allocated GPUs; the inherited `ep_size=8` is not a one-GPU configuration.
Use a supported BF16 precision (`bf16-flash` or `bf16-automodel`), and leave `use_fused_linear_ce=false`.
Packed decoder inputs are supported; packed encoder execution is not enabled by this entry point.

## 3. Configure labels, adaptation, and data

Preserve explicit user choices. Otherwise start with the shipped `dflash.label_source=target_argmax`:
these are the frozen target's greedy next-token labels under the original teacher-forced text/audio context.
They are not generated rollouts or soft-logit distillation. Reference tokens and audio-conditioned features remain
the draft's input context. Validation uses the same label source. Use `ground_truth` to train on the supplied dataset
tokens, whether they are human references or model-generated labels (see the workflow below).

Current recipe defaults are block size **8**, `loss_decay_gamma=4.0`, `num_anchors=512`, and constant AdamW LR **6e-4**.
Block16 or gamma7 are experiment overrides, not repository defaults. Supply `dflash.optimizer` and
`dflash.lr_scheduler` explicitly when an adaptation schedule is wanted; the training guide has an example.
For an extended run, inspect the restored LR and scheduler horizon: increasing `trainer.max_steps` alone does not
redesign the learning-rate schedule. Specify whether a step budget is a total or additional steps.

- **Full-draft adaptation:** `dflash.projection_only=false` (default).
- **Projection-only ablation:** `dflash.projection_only=true` requires DFlash2 and a compatible pretrained draft.
  Only the draft feature projection `fc.weight` trains, not the SALM audio projection. Frozen draft layers still
  transmit gradients to `fc`. Compare against full-draft training with matched data, labels, schedule, and initialization.
- **Block8 to block16:** set `dflash.block_size=16` for a weights-only warm start while preserving the matching
  architecture and taps. Changing block size does not require changing weight shapes. Do not assume projection-only
  adaptation or inference beyond the trained block length will perform as well; measure them.

For packed training, configure `model.packed_sequences=true` and the matching Lhotse token-based sampler
(`use_multimodal_sampling`, `use_packed_sequence_sampling`, `measure_total_length`, `batch_tokens`, and no fixed
`batch_size`). Verify the audio token estimator matches the encoder and chunking. `num_anchors` is per row:
packed THD uses one row per rank; padded BSHD can allocate `batch_size * num_anchors` blocks per rank.
Reduce the token budget or anchor count when memory requires it rather than assuming packing removes draft-logit cost.

For long-audio adaptation, inspect duration filters and actual sampled batches before changing blend weights.
Dataset draw weights are not anchor fractions: long examples supply more eligible token positions.
If targeting a long-audio anchor fraction, define the duration threshold and estimate exposure with the actual
sampler, token budget, block size, and anchor cap. Include short-only batches in the denominator and keep evaluation
data separate. Record estimated exposure as an estimate, not a measured full-run fraction.

### Train DFlash2 from offline model-generated labels

Use this workflow when the user supplies generated transcripts or wants to generate training labels in advance.
It uses the existing dataset-label path; `ground_truth` names that code path and does not require human annotation.

1. Generate transcripts from the training audio, preferably with the same frozen target and prompt used for serving.
   Record the teacher checkpoint, prompt, and decoding settings. Retain sample IDs and exclude failed or truncated
   generations from the training-label artifact until they are repaired. Keep the original references separately.
2. Write a new training manifest with generated text as the supervised assistant response, preserving audio paths,
   offsets, durations, and prompt context. For ordinary `lhotse_as_conversation` ASR input this is the cut's
   `supervisions[0].text` (or NeMo ASR manifest `text` before conversion). For a conversation dataset, replace the
   intended assistant text turns while preserving user/audio turns. Inspect the formatted examples and loss mask;
   custom preference/task adapters can select a different response field.
3. Point the existing data loader at that artifact and select dataset labels. For example, merge this into the
   verified run config; the cuts must retain the prompt context used for generation:

   ```yaml
   dflash:
     variant: dflash2
     label_source: ground_truth
   data:
     train_ds:
       input_cfg:
         - type: lhotse_as_conversation
           cuts_path: /path/to/generated-train-cuts.jsonl.gz
           audio_locator_tag: ${model.audio_locator_tag}
   ```

4. Run the same smoke/resume/export checks as for reference-label training. For draft validation against this teacher,
   prepare a separate held-out generated-label set. Keep human evaluation references for WER and never train on them.

The target still computes audio-conditioned hidden features during training. Generated response tokens provide both
the teacher-forced context and supervision. This differs from `target_argmax`, which recomputes next-token labels
under whatever response context is in the dataset; it would override the supplied labels. No new label-source mode,
separate label-file argument, or cached hidden-state loader is required for offline text labels.

## 4. Smoke, then train

Create a run config such as `examples/speechlm2/conf/dflash_local.yaml` inheriting `dflash` and `_self_`, with the
verified target, draft, data, schedule, and output settings above. Resolve it before submission:

```bash
python examples/speechlm2/dflash_train.py --config-name=dflash_local --cfg job --resolve
```

Check for unresolved data paths and unintended inherited defaults. For a single allocated eight-GPU node, a short
smoke invocation is:

```bash
torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=8 examples/speechlm2/dflash_train.py \
  --config-name=dflash_local \
  trainer.devices=8 trainer.num_nodes=1 trainer.max_steps=25 \
  trainer.limit_train_batches=25 trainer.val_check_interval=25 trainer.limit_val_batches=2 \
  exp_manager.explicit_log_dir=/path/to/new-smoke-run exp_manager.resume_if_exists=false
```

Use a representative held-out validation subset. For multi-node runs, use the site's existing launcher/rendezvous
and set `trainer.num_nodes` to the allocation; do not use independent `--standalone` processes on each node.
Use the project's established source-staging and storage workflow rather than copying a source tree per worker.

Verify finite loss and gradients, the intended trainable parameters, advancing steps, memory, and steady-state step
time after compilation. Check `train/dflash_skipped_step` and its reason metrics: synchronized skips advance training
without learning from those batches. Confirm validation processes valid anchors; an all-skipped epoch logs
`val_acc=0` to satisfy checkpoint monitoring and is not evidence of useful validation.

For a new distributed recipe, include checkpoint save/restore and HF export reload in the smoke test. Verify the
resumed step and LR, and that all expected distributed checkpoint shards exist. Scale to the requested run after
these checks pass. Monitor progress from logs/checkpoints, not queue state alone. On repeated failure, diagnose the
first failing rank and data/storage access before retrying; retain the last known good checkpoint.

## 5. Export and measure acceptance

`SALMDFlashModule.on_train_end` writes a draft-only HF export to `dflash.output_dir`; a relative path resolves under
`trainer.log_dir`. An interrupted job may have a resumable checkpoint without that final export. Verify which step
an export represents and strictly reload it with the matching draft class before serving it with the frozen target.
Retain the resumable checkpoint when further training is planned.

Follow the serving guide for the installed vLLM/plugin pair. DFlash2 uses speculative `method="dflash"`; confirm the
DFlash2 architecture/selector is actually selected. Start with `num_speculative_tokens=block_size-1` for a matched
training/inference block. Smaller K is a separate inference evaluation; K proposals plus one visible anchor make
a runtime block of K+1 positions. Do not rewrite the export architecture to bypass serving compatibility checks.

Compare baseline and adapted drafts on identical sample IDs, target, prompts, decoding limits, precision, K, and
scoring. Include both long- and short-form data when changing the training duration mix. Validate greedy outputs
against target-only inference and report WER, throughput/latency, and acceptance; higher acceptance alone is not
proof of higher serving throughput or unchanged transcription quality.

For the convention that includes the target/bonus token, aggregate **MAL = 1 + accepted draft tokens / draft rounds**
from counters scoped to the measured requests. Report K and the counter definition; do not average per-job MAL
without weighting by draft rounds. For per-position acceptance, distinguish accepted-at-position / proposed-at-position
from conditional acceptance given that the earlier prefix survived. Training `accept_len` is teacher-forced and
does not substitute for serving MAL.

Record evaluated/expected sample counts, failures, truncations, concurrency, and export step with every result.
Retry failed samples under the same settings and preserve their IDs. Do not combine rerun counters with an original
run's failed partial-generation counters unless those partial contributions can be excluded; label any mixed-run
aggregate as provisional when exact attribution is unavailable.

# Training a speech LLM from pretrained components

This skill turns a pretrained LLM and pretrained speech encoders into one SALM model and trains it end to end. The run
uses a weighted multitask blend, tens of thousands of steps and tens of nodes. The procedure is written for a hybrid
Mamba-attention MoE LLM such as Nemotron 3 Nano, and most of it applies to any backbone.

- `examples/speechlm2/conf/salm_nemotron.yaml` is the annotated starting config. Start from it rather than from
  `salm_automodel.yaml`, whose portable defaults are slow at this scale.
- `examples/speechlm2/salm_train.py` trains the model, and `examples/speechlm2/to_hf.py` exports a checkpoint for
  vLLM.
- `.claude/skills/migrate-to-resumable-dataloader/` sets up indexed, resumable data loading, which this skill
  requires.
- `.claude/skills/debug-training-logs/` finds the root cause when a distributed job dies.

Two terms recur throughout. A **source** is one leaf entry of the data blend, and a **draw** is one example sampled
from a source.

## The governing risk: silent damage

A run of this size costs tens of thousands of GPU-hours. The failures that waste it rarely crash. They surface
thousands of steps later as an evaluation regression, and by then the only fix is a fork from an earlier checkpoint.
Every check in this skill guards against one of them:

| What you notice | Actual cause | Caught by |
|---|---|---|
| Insertions climb and WER drifts upward over thousands of steps | `precision: bf16-true` cast the LLM's FP32 tensors (Mamba, router) to BF16 | Step 4, dtype check |
| WER swings between neighboring checkpoints, with many empty outputs | A "non-speech" source contained real speech labeled with an empty answer, so the model learned to stop early | Step 2, audits |
| After a restart, examples are garbled or mismatched | A manifest changed after its index was built | Step 2, immutable data |
| A source contributes nothing, and no error appears | Wrong source `type` or a missing `text_field`, so every draw is dropped | Step 4, loss-token probe |
| Long examples never appear in training | `max_tokens` filters examples out; it does not cap them | Step 3 |
| A fork resumes from its parent's latest step instead of the requested one | The fork reused the parent's log directory, and `resume_if_exists` overrode `resume_from_checkpoint` | Step 5 |

None of these raises an error. Do not launch a run, or resume one after any change, without Steps 2 and 4.

## Step 1: Assemble the model

- **LLM.** Use a chat checkpoint and its matching `prompt_format` (`nemotron-nano-v3` for Nemotron 3 Nano). The
  formatter prepends an empty `<think></think>` to every training answer, so serve with `enable_thinking=false`.
- **Speech encoders.** `pe_encoder_path` mounts a parallel-expert encoder: an ASR encoder and a diarization encoder
  side by side, fused per frame, so one model handles both single- and multi-speaker transcription. It replaces the
  encoder of `pretrained_asr`, which still supplies the preprocessor. Use the same feature normalization
  (`asr_normalize_type`, `diar_normalize_type`) in training and serving: a mismatch moves WER and produces no other
  symptom. Without a speaker branch, drop `pe_encoder_path` and `data.multispeaker_cfg`.
- **Chunking and packing.** With `encoder_chunk_size_seconds: 30`, the encoders handle long recordings at the cost
  and memory of short ones. A transformer or parallel-expert encoder also accepts packed input
  (`packed_encoder_sequences`), which removes encoder padding. Mirror the encoder's front end and subsampling in
  `audio_token_estimator`.
- **Connector.** `IdentityConnector` passes encoder states unchanged to perception's single linear projection into the
  LLM's hidden size. Its `d_model` must equal the encoder's output width.
- **Multi-token prediction.** Train two MTP layers jointly with the backbone. They cost little during training and
  speed up serving through speculative decoding. Configure them only under `model.mtp`. The legacy top-level
  `compute_mtp` flag has no effect on training.
- **Checkpoints.** Download the HF checkpoints into the cluster's shared cache before the first job, so that hundreds
  of ranks do not download them at once.

## Step 2: Build the data blend

### Structure

Each entry in `input_cfg` has a type that decides how its rows become conversations:

- `lhotse_as_conversation` turns speech rows into `[system, context, audio] → answer`. Its `preference_sampling`
  option handles rows that carry several alternative targets: it draws one task per row according to fixed task
  weights. Set `skip_invalid_target: true` so that rows lacking the drawn target are skipped rather than trained
  with an empty answer. `preference_sampling` has no effect under any other type.
- `group` nests a blend whose data is already in conversation form, such as multi-speaker data or text-only chat.

`tags` overwrite fields of the same name (`context`, `system_prompt`) on every row of their source.

### Weights

**Weight sources by the answer tokens they contribute to the loss, not by hours or rows.** Sources differ by more
than ten times in supervised tokens per draw. A short contextual-ASR answer and a long multi-speaker transcript are
one draw each, so weights based on hours or rows misallocate the gradient.

1. Measure `a_i`, the mean answer tokens per draw, for every source. Measure through the real training path: indexed
   reader, preference sampling, prompt formatter and loss mask. Sample at least 1,000 rows per source and require
   zero errors.
2. Choose each source's target share `t_i` of all answer tokens. Temperature 0.5 is a good default:
   `t_i ∝ m_i^0.5`, where `m_i` is the source's total answer tokens. Give capability-retention data, such as
   text-only chat, a small explicit share instead.
3. Set each draw weight to `w_i ∝ t_i / a_i`, and normalize within every list of siblings.
4. Measure again whenever a source's content, prompt or task weights change. Weights are valid only for the blend
   revision they were measured on.

### Audits

Audit every source before it joins a blend:

- **Empty or very short targets.** Run an independent ASR model on a random sample drawn from many shards. Corpora
  labeled "non-speech" often contain intelligible speech. Trained with an empty answer, such an example supervises
  only EOS, and the model learns to stop before transcribing.
- **Schema.** Check that the expected `text_field` is present, that sample rates match, and that multi-speaker rows
  respect `num_speakers`.
- **Access.** From inside the training container and as the training user, read a sample from across the source, not
  only its first record. Every path prefix in the manifests must be mounted.

### Immutability

An index pack holds the precomputed indexes that let the dataloader resume a source exactly; a pack root is the
directory of packs for one blend. Freeze the manifests first, then build their packs into a new pack root for each
blend revision. Build into a temporary directory and rename it to its final path when complete. A weight-only change
can reuse existing packs. A content change needs a new blend revision, rebuilt packs, re-measured weights and a new
config file. Never rebuild a pack that a running job reads.

## Step 3: Configure

`salm_nemotron.yaml` encodes the settings below. They decide speed, stability and whether data goes missing silently.

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `trainer.precision` | `bf16-automodel` | Automodel owns parameter dtypes, so FP32 tensors stay FP32. Never use `bf16-true`. |
| `model.optimizer` | TE `FusedAdam` with FP32 master weights and BF16 moments | Halves optimizer-state memory and keeps update precision |
| `model.lr_scheduler` | Cosine decay after a linear warmup | Retune the peak rate for each backbone and global batch size |
| `data.train_ds.batch_tokens` | 65,536 per rank | Exact with `use_packed_sequence_sampling` and `measure_total_length` |
| `data.train_ds.max_tokens` | equal to `batch_tokens` | It is a filter. A lower value silently drops long examples. |
| `data.train_ds.use_bucketing` | `false` | Packing already removes padding, so bucketing only correlates batches |
| `data.train_ds.audio_token_estimator` | mirrors the encoder front end | Exact packing needs it to count audio tokens |
| `model.packed_sequences` | `true` | The LLM sees examples concatenated without padding. Set `packed_encoder_sequences` too when the encoder supports it. |
| `model.cross_entropy_backend` | `fused_linear` | Never materializes full-vocabulary logits |
| `model.automodel_backend` | TE attention and linear layers, grouped-GEMM experts, DeepEP dispatcher | Treat as fixed. Never fall back to `torch` kernels to debug. |
| `trainer.strategy` | 8-way expert parallelism, FSDP across all ranks, activation checkpointing in LLM and perception | Fits 80 GB GPUs at 65,536 tokens per rank |
| `model.train_gate` | `true` | Lets the MoE router adapt to speech. `aux_loss_coeff` applies only when above 0; a value of 0 keeps the checkpoint's coefficient rather than disabling the loss. |
| `data.train_ds.indexed`, `use_stateful_dataloader`, `index_pack_root` | on, with an immutable pack root | Restores the exact data order after every restart |
| `exp_manager.checkpoint_callback_params` | every 500 steps, `save_top_k: -1` | Keeps every checkpoint for selection by decoding |
| `exp_manager.max_time_per_run` | a few minutes under the job's wall-time limit | Leaves time for the final distributed checkpoint save |

Model-config keys that no code reads are ignored silently, and unknown data keys only log a warning. After adding or
renaming a key, find the code that reads it in the exact source tree you package for the job.

## Step 4: Preflight

1. **Loss-token probe.** Pass 50 to 100 rows from each source through the real dataset, formatter and collator, and
   print the decoded loss-bearing tokens. Every assistant turn must be supervised and nothing else may be. No source
   may produce EOS as its only target, unless it is true non-speech that passed the audit.
2. **Single-node smoke test.** Run 100 to 200 steps with the production container and code, scaled down to one node.
   At load, there must be no missing-key or dropped-tensor warnings. During training, require finite loss,
   `packing_efficiency` near 1.0 and peak memory with a few GiB of headroom. A single node does not predict
   multi-node step time.
3. **Dtype check.** Read the metadata of the first saved distributed checkpoint. Every tensor that the HF checkpoint
   stores in FP32 must still be FP32. Repeat the check after any change to precision settings or to Automodel.
4. **Restart check.** Stop the smoke run after a save and resume it. The log must show that the optimizer, scheduler,
   RNG and dataloader states were restored, and training must continue from the saved step.

Point `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` and `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` at shared storage and warm them once with the production
image. Otherwise every job spends minutes compiling kernels before its first step.

## Step 5: Launch

- **Chain jobs.** Submit the run as a chain of jobs, each within the wall-time limit. Each job saves a checkpoint when
  its timer expires. A job can still exit with an error after that save, for example from a crash during teardown,
  and an `afterok` dependency then cancels the rest of the chain. Chain with `afterany` and confirm each job's save.
  To stop the run, cancel every queued job; a forgotten `afterany` job keeps training.
- **Fork from a specific step.** `resume_if_exists` resumes from the `-last` checkpoint in the log directory and
  overrides `resume_from_checkpoint`. To fork from step N, give the fork a new `explicit_log_dir` and set
  `resume_from_checkpoint` to the parent's `step=N` checkpoint.
- **Exclude bad nodes.** Keep a list of nodes to exclude and re-check it before every launch. Typical offenders are a
  GPU that fails at startup, a thermally throttled GPU that doubles step time, and a faulty network link that triggers
  NCCL watchdog timeouts.
- **Crashes that repeat at the same step.** A crash that recurs at the same step on every attempt depends on that
  step's data or on the parallel layout. Inspect the batch, then try a different layout before retrying. A crash that
  does not recur only needs a resume.

## Step 6: Monitor

Take the step time, dataloader wait and memory of the first stable hour as the baseline. Expect the first hour after
each resume to run slower while caches warm up.

| Signal | Act when |
|---|---|
| Step time, rolling median | It stays above 1.5 times the baseline for more than 30 minutes. With healthy loss, look for a slow node. |
| Dataloader wait | It grows from tens of milliseconds toward a second. Suspect storage, I/O or too few workers. |
| Per-rank memory and utilization | One rank differs from the rest. Suspect a straggler. |
| Loss and MTP loss | A spike appears. Resume from the previous checkpoint and see whether it recurs at the same step; a spike that does not recur is noise. |

Read the current step from the rank-zero log. Logger dashboards can lag behind it, and epoch or batch counters do not
equal the optimizer step.

## Step 7: Evaluate and select checkpoints

**Accept a checkpoint before evaluating it.** Require two identical file listings taken a few minutes apart, no
temporary or zero-byte files, a passing dtype check, and at least one finite training step after the save. Evaluate
the numbered `step=N` checkpoint. The `-last` checkpoint is overwritten as training continues.

**Select checkpoints by decoding, never by loss.** Export with `to_hf.py`, serve with vLLM, and score the full
benchmark suite:

- Use MTP speculative decoding. With vLLM 0.32 or newer, serve with `--use-replayssm --mamba-backend flashinfer
  --mamba-cache-mode none --no-enable-prefix-caching`. The older `--mamba-cache-mode all` setting is no longer
  available.
- Serving pads the vocabulary, and its untrained rows can outscore every real token. The NeMo vLLM plugin masks them
  (`speechlm_output_vocab_size`); replicate that mask if you serve with another stack. Count `<|audio|>` tokens and
  empty outputs in every evaluation.
- Report insertions, deletions and empty outputs, not only WER. The silent failures above first show up in these
  counts.
- Score a text-only benchmark as well, to catch regressions in the LLM's text capability.
- Compare checkpoints across the whole suite. Neighboring checkpoints fluctuate, so a single benchmark cannot pick a
  winner.

A model that learned to stop early cannot be repaired at decode time. Forcing a first token recovers the affected
utterances but also breaks correct abstention on true non-speech. Remove the bad data and continue training; a later
RL stage that rewards complete transcripts can also correct the remaining early stops.

## Step 8: Change a run in flight

Fork from an accepted checkpoint into a new log directory and a new config revision. A full-state resume restores the
optimizer, scheduler and dataloader states along with the weights.

| Change | How | Never |
|---|---|---|
| Learning rate or schedule | New config, full-state resume | Edit a config that a queued job will read |
| Source weights | New weights on the same packs, full-state resume | Reweight without measuring answer tokens again |
| Add a source | Declare likely future sources from the start with weight `0.0`, then raise the weight | Insert a new entry into a running blend: the saved dataloader state no longer matches it |
| Remove a source | Set its weight to `0.0` | Delete its entry, which misaligns the saved dataloader state |
| Fix a source's content | New pack root, re-measured weights, new revision | Rebuild a pack in place |

Make one change per fork, name its parent, and compare the two at matched steps under an identical evaluation setup.
A change usually improves its target benchmarks while moving unrelated ones. Adopt it only after scoring the full
suite.

content:
---
name: verify
description: Verify a NeMo Speech change or pull request before commit, push, or review by checking the complete diff, formatting, tests, documentation, and DCO sign-offs. Use when asked to verify changes, prepare a commit or PR, or review a PR's validation and coverage.
---

Verify the current change proportionally to its risk. Do not report success for checks that were not run.

1. **Establish the complete scope.** Inspect committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes:

   ```bash
   git status --short
   git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD
   git diff --name-only
   git diff --cached --name-only
   ```

   Replace `origin/main` if the PR targets another branch. Read the full diff and any applicable nested `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` files.

2. **Review tests and documentation.** Before running commands, determine whether the change is adequately covered:

   - Require a regression test for a bug fix and focused unit tests for new or changed behavior, including important edge cases. If no test is appropriate, require a concrete explanation.
   - Check whether changes to public APIs, configuration, CLI behavior, examples, or user workflows are reflected in the relevant documentation. If no documentation update is needed, record why.
   - Self-review the diff against the `/review` rubric (`.claude/skills/nemo-speech-pr-review/SKILL.md`) and fix blocking and should-fix items before requesting review.

3. **Run repository checks.** For staged changes, run:

   ```bash
   pre-commit run
   ```

   For committed branch changes, run `pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`. If pre-commit is unavailable, use `uvx pre-commit` for the same command. Review and stage hook fixes, then rerun until clean. Also run `git diff --check`.

4. **Run the smallest relevant tests.** Prefer focused test files or test names while iterating, then expand to the affected collection when practical:

   - `nemo/collections/asr/` → `uv run pytest tests/collections/asr -m "not pleasefixme"`
   - `nemo/collections/tts/` → `uv run pytest tests/collections/tts -m "not pleasefixme"`
   - `nemo/collections/audio/` → `uv run pytest tests/collections/audio -m "not pleasefixme"`
   - `nemo/collections/speechlm2/` → `uv run pytest tests/collections/speechlm2 -m "not pleasefixme"`
   - `nemo/collections/common/` → `uv run pytest tests/collections/common -m "not pleasefixme"`
   - `nemo/core/` → `uv run pytest tests/core -m "not pleasefixme"`

   Add `--with_downloads` only for tests marked as requiring model downloads. Use `--cpu` when supported and a GPU is unavailable. If documentation changed, install its dependencies with `uv sync --locked --group docs` and build it with `uv run make -C docs html`.

5. **Verify commit sign-offs.** Every commit in the PR must have a DCO `Signed-off-by` trailer:

   ```bash
   git log --format='%h %s%n%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by)' origin/main..HEAD
   ```

   Create commits with `git commit -s`. Add a missing trailer to your own latest commit with `git commit --amend --no-edit -s`; do not rewrite other contributors' commits without authorization.

6. **Report results.** Summarize the reviewed diff, test-coverage and documentation conclusions, exact commands and outcomes, commit sign-off status, and any skipped checks with reasons. For failures, include the relevant error and a concrete next step.
